newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs seen steady-up $0.50 - trade.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs seen steady-up $0.50 - trade.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices on Tuesday were seen steady to $0.50 per cwt higher, supported by expected light hog marketings and outlooks for imrproved pork demand, dealers and packer buyers said.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota top prices on hogs delivered at plants were seen ranging from $48.00 to $48.50, sources there said.
Illinois top prices at plants also could range $48.00 to $48.50, Illinois dealers said.
Indiana/Ohio hog prices at the plant could range $48.50 to $49.00, dealers and packer buyers said.

Early support to cash hog prices was generated by lighter-than-expected interior Iowa/southern Minnesota hog movement over the weekend and packers who bid higher to secure enough hogs for Monday's slaughter, dealers said.

Interior movement on Friday came in at 97,000 head compared with estimates of 100,000 and Saturday's movement was 19,000 versus the estimate of 25,000, USDA statistics showed. Monday's movement was pegged at 100,000 head, well below 110,000 a week ago and 114,000 a year ago.
Light support also was tied to ideas that retail buying for pre-Easter promotions would turn pork prices higher.
